newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson seen on course for more growth.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson seen on course for more growth.

text.p: LM Ericsson AB Tuesday reported a 30 percent jump in nine month profits which boosted hopes that the Swedish telecommunications giant would ring up further growth, led by its mobile phone unit.

Ericsson reported a nine month pre-tax profit of 6.26 billion Swedisn crowns ($954 million) against 4.81 billion ($733 million) a year ago but warned that increasing competition in the global telecommunications sector could impact profit margins.

The company said order bookings had risen 22 percent in the nine months to 95.6 billion crowns ($14.6 billion) and net sales by 17 percent to 78.20 billion crowns ($11.9 billion) -- largely due to its mobile phone unit.

Analysts were expecting the strong trend in order bookings to continue in the fourth quarter. Chief Executive Lars Ramqvist told a news conference order bookings could reach 130 billion crowns ($19.8 billion) for the full year.
The highlight of the report was the radio communications division that includes the company's mobile telephone business and accounted for over 63 percent of sales.
Lars Ramqvist said sales of mobile phones and systems jumped 38 percent in the nine months to Sept. 30 and order bookings rose 34 percent.
"This means that Ericsson is strengthening its market position," Ramqvist said in a statement.
However he sounded a warning that competition at the cutting edge of mobile telephones could hit profit margins.
U.S. rival Motorala Inc. posted weaker third quarter results earlier this month, partly blaming competitive pressures and continuing price declines in cellular telephones.
